newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa stoppages set for Thursday - union.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa stoppages set for Thursday - union.

text.p: German airline Deutsche Lufthansa AG will face a two-hour stoppage by its workers at a number of airports across the country starting at 0530 GMT on Thursday, German union DAG said on Wednesday.
DAG, in a long-running pay dispute with Lufthansa, last month held brief stoppages that cost the airline some 12 million marks ($7.8 million) as 35 flights had to be cancelled.

"The (scheduled) protest action is a consequence of the unwillingness of the Lufthansa board to change their position in the negotiations that last took place on Monday," DAG chief negotiator Michael Tarp said in a statement.
DAG said the walk-outs would involve Lufthansa airstaff and groundstaff at airports in Frankfurt, Hamburg, Munich, Duesseldorf and Hanover.
A two-hour work interruption is the maximum permitted under German labour law until conditions allowing full strikes to go ahead have been satisfied.
Sources close to airline staff said on Tuesday the protests are likely to hit international traffic next time as well as the domestic traffic involved in the first protest.
They added that if Lufthansa refused to change its position as a result, a ballot on all-out strike action could follow.

DAG, which shares representation of the airline's 50,000 staff with the transport and public sector union OeTV, has said Lufthansa has still not offered its members a 1997 wage increase in line with others in the industry.

It is also angry that Lufthansa wants the new contracts to last 27 months instead of a year. Given the threat that many Lufthansa jobs could be moved abroad, the union would not tie itself to a two-year contract, DAG has said.
Lufthansa described the scheduled protest as "completely incomprehensible" and said that such a move would not force it to alter its position.
